Normally, in a methodology class, you read theoretical, dry, and often non-practice-oriented texts that can feel detached from the actual craft of doing history. Since these courses are usually centered on theory and methodological debates, the practical gains can sometimes be limited. This course was the exact opposite. By engaging in discussions under Professor Luca’s guidance, particularly in the areas of his expertise, we practiced a form of history that was less abstract and far more lively and hands-on.

In short, Professor Luca essentially invites you into his own historiographical “kitchen” and shows you firsthand how history is actually done. It is an unusual method, but compared to the more conventional approach, it was much more dynamic, exciting, and enjoyable. Even though my own field of study is quite different from Professor Luca’s, I was still able to learn a great deal from him by knowing how to make the most of the experience. This course and Professor Luca will stay in my memories for a lifetime. Thanks Bilkent!

Prof Luca is very passionate about the subject matter and is very knowledgeable about various ideas and evolving interpretations. However, the course was too challenging for non-archaeology students, who do not possess adequate background knowledge or training in archaeology. The lectures were not as well structured to facilitate students' understanding and flow of ideas and developments. As such, the content grasped by students tended to be piecemeal and random, rather than structured to provide at least a broad, even if not deep, overview about Byzantine and Islamic art and archaeology. Additionally, due to time constraints, I do not think Islamic art and archaeology was covered in the course. The group presentations/discussions on readings are a solid assessment mode but Prof tended to have a clear template or answer scheme or expected answers in mind from students, even though he mentions that the assignment is meant to be geared as much as possible to students' interpretations. Perhaps, providing some basic expectations from the readings in the form of guiding questions for the groups might help to tighten the expected focus from these presentations. Additionally, the final research paper, while useful for senior undergraduates, demands some fundamental training/background in the field of study, not applicable to those who are not from archaeology. Perhaps, a better way to accommodate the diversity in class is to provide the choice of choosing from a list of essay questions (for non-archaeology students) or pursuing a personal research topic (for the archaeology students). Other than that, Prof Luca is very lively and entertaining, which makes his lessons worth attending on a regular basis :)

Luca genel olarak iyi niyetli ve pozitif bir insan ancak bu ders için uygun bir hoca olduğunu düşünmüyorum. Modern Europe hakkında bilgili olsa da dönemin uzmanı olmadığını özellikle Rönesans ve Reform gibi Early Modern Europe konularını geçtikten sonra hissediyorsunuz. Koskoca tarih bölümünde böyle bir dersi verebilecek uzmanın olmaması da ayrı trajik! Luca'nın en olumlu yanı ise öğretmenlik becerileriyle ilgili. Hemen hemen bütün öğrencilerini isimleriyle tanır ve derse etkin bir şekilde katılabilmeleri için elinden geleni yapar. Zaman zaman esprilerinin dozunu kaçırıp ciddiyetini kaybetse de, bunun tamamen soğuk ve donuk olmaktan daha iyi olduğu kanaatindeyim. Ayrıca midterm'leri biraz daha bonkör bir şekilde okusa zararına olmaz.
course: Ders modern Avrupa konusunda, temel niteliğinde almanız gereken bilgi ve analiz becerilerini size kazandırıyor ancak Luca'nın müfredatı dizayn ediş biçiminden kaynaklanan ufak tefek sorunlar olabiliyor. Örneğin, zaman zaman fazlaca gereksiz detaylarda boğulabiliyorsunuz (bunlarda fazlaca uzun yazılarla dolu ve öğrencilerle paylaşmadığı slaytların payı büyük). Bu detaylara gereksiz diyorum çünkü haftalık ortalama 3 saatlik bir derste tüm bu detaylara zaman harcanırsa konuları bitirmek imkansızlaşacaktır. İkincisi, ders economic determinism ve Marxist historiography klişelerine fazlaca bağlı kalınarak işleniyor. Bu eminim ki herkes için olumsuz bir detay olmayacaktır fakat modern Avrupa'daki ekonomik dönüşümleri gerektiği gibi kavrarken, siyasi, diplomatik ve sosyal değişimleri anlamakta zorluk yaşıyorsunuz.
